text:
maya: Heads up — saw a production spike where fncall schema rejects jumped and a bunch of tool invocations were routed to the degen path. Console shows a sudden quota burn. cc @raj @tammy :grimacing:

alex: Oh no. Which validator did we have in the canary? strict or soft?

maya: strict (canary rollout started yesterday morning). The rejects are mostly small JSON shape mismatches (missing optional metadata) but routing logic classified them as hard rejects and sent to degen.

raj: Do we have logs for an example?

maya: pasted one snippet from the router logs: ```
2026-03-22T09:12:03Z ERROR route=eu-west-1 route_id=validator-strict fncall=tool.fax_send status=REJECT reason=SchemaMismatch details="missing field: user_locale"
2026-03-22T09:12:03Z INFO reroute=degen route_id=degen-fallback billing_tag=charged
```

sam: That `billing_tag=charged` is the problem — degen should be free/never-charge in this case. Looks like the routing-policy map didn't include the `validation:softfallthrough` tag.

tammy: Confirmed — policy matrix for strict validator had `on_reject: reroute` but no explicit `charge: false` override. Edge case where enforcement->reroute caused a billable path.

alex: Hmm. Two separate issues: 1) validator strict is too aggressive on optional fields, 2) reroute path has incorrect charge semantics. Which one do we address first?

raj: Short-term: flip the canary back to soft for strict-validator rollout and patch the routing policy to avoid billing on degen reroutes. Long-term: we should tighten the validator rules and add a sampling rule to not count rerouted rejects as billable until validated.

maya: I agree. I can rollback the canary now. Command: `/rollout set validator:fncall-validation=soft-canary --id=canary-42`

deploy-bot: @maya received request to set validator:fncall-validation -> soft-canary (canary-42). Applying...

deploy-bot: Done. Change deployed to 40% of traffic.

sam: Thanks. I'll open a quick policy patch: add `charge: false` to degen paths for any validation reroute. Patch in git: `platform/routers/policies/validator_reroute.yaml` with: ```yaml
- name: reroute-degen-on-validate
  match: { reason: SchemaMismatch }
  action: { reroute: degen-fallback, charge: false }
```

tammy: Nice. Also can we get a console dashboard panel that shows "reroute_count" vs "billed_reroute_count"? We should detect when they diverge > 0.5% and auto-alert.

alex: +1. Add an alert that pages on high divergence during a rollout window. It should include the active route_id and the validator id.

raj: For follow-up: add a sampling flag so that we store the original reject reason in the trace even after reroute. That will make audits easier and prevent misattribution.

maya: Action items: 1) maya rolled canary to soft (done) 2) sam will PR policy patch (ETA 2h) 3) tammy will add dashboard panel & alert (ETA EOD) 4) raj will spec a trace sampling field for reroutes (ETA next week).

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4921 — small YAML change + unit test for charge behavior.

tammy: Dashboard query I plan to add: `sum(reroute_total) by (route_id)`, `sum(billed_reroute_total) by (route_id)` then `delta = billed / reroute` — alert if delta > 0.005. Drafting now.

alex: Once sam's patch merges, let's run a short synthetic test to ensure reroutes don't bill: call a fncall with intentionally missing optional field and watch billing tag in logs.

maya: Good plan. Also let's add a note to the release rollouts doc: "validator canaries that reroute should not be billed; if billing occurs, rollback immediately."

raj: I'll take that doc update.

sam: Quick question — do we need to backfill customers who were billed incorrectly? How many hits are we talking about?

maya: Early estimate: ~1.8k rerouted calls over 45 minutes across 3 accounts. Rough cost impact low but we should offer credits if customers complain. 

tammy: I'll prepare a support template and tagging guidance for CS.

alex: Thanks all. After the patch and dashboard are in, let's re-run the strict validator canary but with a small percentage and the new alert on.

maya: Agreed. Closing the loop: can we decide on the gating for re-enabling strict? Proposal: require reroute_billed_ratio < 0.1% over 30m and no customer complaints.

raj: Fine by me.

sam: I'll monitor logs while the PR lands. ping me if anything odd. :thumbsup:
